# BrighTO-Router

BrighTO-Router is a free, open-source, self-hosted LLM gateway, AI router, model router, model load balancer, and SystemOne decision router written in Rust.

Official repository: https://github.com/thusinh1969/BrighTO_Router
Official Docker image: thusinh1969/brighto_airouter:v1.3.0
License: Apache-2.0
Author: Nguyễn Anh Nguyên, BrighTO AI, nguyen@hatto.com

## What it does

BrighTO-Router gives teams one stable API endpoint for OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic-compatible, cloud, local, Ollaya/Laya, and JEV/DJEV-style System One backends. It supports Chat Completions, legacy Completions, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages, embeddings, rerank, ASR/transcription, SystemOne decisions, team API keys, token budgets, usage logging, and NGINX-style Model Groups for round-robin or weighted load balancing. An explicit Claude CLI bridge lets an OpenAI Chat route also accept Anthropic Messages at /v1/messages, so Claude Code can use an OpenAI-compatible model without a separate native Anthropic backend.

The single-file brighto.py Python SDK covers every public inference endpoint. test_router.py uses the same SDK for command-line checks. Setup and method examples: https://thusinh1969.github.io/BrighTO_Router/API_EXAMPLES.html

Quyết by Chinh Nguyen (https://github.com/ncchinh/quyet) is an independent decision-model runtime with the System One response contract. An optional external HTTP example serves it behind BrighTO; it is not bundled into the Rust router image.

Native agent clients can use matching protocol routes: Claude Code through Anthropic Messages (native or the explicit OpenAI Chat bridge), Codex through OpenAI Responses, and Hermes/OpenClaw through Chat Completions. Streaming tool calls and results are forwarded; apart from the explicit Claude CLI bridge, BrighTO does not convert protocols automatically. Upstream compatibility and tool calling are required. Configuration, model-name caveat, and verified-version scope: https://thusinh1969.github.io/BrighTO_Router/AGENT_CLIENTS.html

## Why it exists

The goal is a narrow, fast, understandable self-hosted LLM traffic path: one Rust binary, one Docker image, PostgreSQL as the durable control-plane and usage store, and no Redis requirement for version 1.3.0.

## Release 1.3.0

1.3.0 adds the explicit Claude CLI bridge: an OpenAI Chat route can also accept Anthropic Messages at /v1/messages, with request/response/stream/tool translation, usage, errors, and a local count_tokens estimate. The same public model keeps serving /v1/chat/completions. Local Qwen 3.8 and other OpenAI-compatible Chat routes can be exposed to Claude Code as an opt-in route option. It requires additive migration 0008; run `./start.sh migrate` before starting the 1.3.0 binary. Runbook: https://thusinh1969.github.io/BrighTO_Router/MIGRATION_0008.html

The previous 1.2.0 security release added constant-time admin key checks, per-source-IP admin auth rate limiting, hardened Portal response headers, explicit client-key reveal, LAN-aware health probes, correct large aliased-request handling, and usage filter correctness.

## Benchmark summary

Benchmarks use deterministic local Rust mock backends and measure router overhead, not model inference speed. Published 1.0/1.1 artifacts include million-token HTTP and HTTPS pass-through tests plus Model Group round-robin and weighted load-balancing tests.

## Privacy posture

BrighTO-Router records metadata for usage analytics, such as tokens, route, provider, status, latency, and error class. It does not log prompt text, uploaded media, tool payloads, or model answers by design.
